text: Discipline Positioning:The major of Municipal Environment and Public Health is an interdisciplinary field that combines engineering and medicine, focusing on environmental governance and public health security in urban infrastructure construction. The duration of study is usually four years, and a Bachelor of Engineering degree is awarded. Some institutions also offer a degree in Management in combination with the direction of public health management.Core features: Based on municipal engineering (such as water supply and drainage, garbage treatment) as the technical foundation and public health (such as epidemiology, environmental hygiene) as the theoretical orientation, it addresses the issues related to the urban environment and human health (such as drinking water safety, the impact of air pollution on health).Interdisciplinary nature：Integrating knowledge from multiple disciplines such as environmental engineering, preventive medicine, management, and law, for example:Treat urban sewage with engineering technology (environmental engineering), and at the same time analyze the impact of water quality on residents' health (public health).
